36549845.dataset_size: 246 patients (training); 200 additional for norms; 9 pathologic cases for testing
36549845.headline_result: Median Dice 0.95 (intracranial), 0.90 (brain); Pearson r=0.996 vs. manual volumes; 8/9 pathologic cases flagged as >2 SD from normative mean

36554113.model_family: CNN (inception residual encoder with dense spatial attention)
36554113.clinical_problem: Can an automatic multi-tissue segmentation model accurately delineate fetal brain tissue types on MRI and estimate gestational age, for neurodevelopmental assessment in healthy and congenitally abnormal fetuses?
36554113.patient_population: 80 pathological and non-pathological fetal brain MRI volumes, gestational ages 20-33 weeks
36554113.model_description: Takes multi-view fetal brain MRI as input; an inception-residual CNN with dense spatial attention outputs seven-tissue-category segmentation; separate modules (3D autoencoder, radiomics, or the segmentation encoder) predict gestational age.
36554113.headline_result: Segmentation Dice 0.791+/-0.18; radiomics-based GA prediction RMSE 1.42

36589836.exclusion_reason: adult population studied (imaging performed in adulthood on individuals born preterm), not pediatric imaging despite preterm birth history

39354975.clinical_problem: Can a deep learning model automatically delineate pediatric brain tumors on combined [18F]FET PET and MRI as accurately as manual expert delineation, to reduce inter-rater variability in tumor volume and treatment response assessment?
39354975.model_description: Takes combined [18F]FET PET and MRI images as input; an ANN outputs automatic delineation (segmentation) of pediatric CNS tumors, from which biological tumor volume and tumor-to-background ratios are calculated.
39354975.headline_result: Median Dice 0.93; clinical metrics correlation r>=0.99 vs. manual reference

33399980.clinical_problem: Can an object detection AI model identify rickets on pediatric wrist radiographs using a small dataset and modest computing resources?
33399980.patient_population: Children younger than 7 years old evaluated for rickets, Children's Healthcare of Atlanta
33399980.model_description: Takes pediatric wrist radiographs as input; an object detection model outputs a labeled bounding box identifying rickets-related metaphyseal changes vs. normal.
33399980.dataset_size: 425 wrists total (104 rickets + 264 normal training; 20 rickets + 37 normal test)
33399980.headline_result: Overall accuracy 86%; sensitivity 80%/specificity 95% for rickets, sensitivity 89%/specificity 90% for normal

33604878.exclusion_reason: adult-focused neuroimaging review with only brief pediatric mention; machine learning discussed only briefly and described as disappointing, not the study's focus

33663479.clinical_problem: Can NLP models classify Norwegian pediatric CT radiology reports as containing abnormal findings versus normal, for quality assurance purposes?
33663479.patient_population: 13,506 pediatric CT reports; also tested on 1,000 adult CT and 1,000 adult X-ray reports
33663479.model_description: Takes free-text Norwegian radiology reports as input; CNN, bi-LSTM, and SVM models output a binary classification of whether the report describes abnormal findings.
33663479.dataset_size: 13,506 pediatric CT reports (plus 1,000 adult CT and 1,000 adult X-ray reports for generalization testing)
33663479.headline_result: CNN best on children's CT: AUC 0.981, F1 0.930

33714842.clinical_problem: Can an automated method correctly align and orient pediatric X-ray images across many body regions to standardize archived studies and support downstream computer-aided diagnosis tools?
33714842.patient_population: Pediatric X-ray images (test sets of 200 and 4,221 images) across 21 body regions
33714842.model_description: Takes pediatric X-ray images as input; a PCA-based alignment stage plus a VGG16 CNN orientation-classification stage outputs correctly aligned and oriented radiographs for standardized archiving and downstream CAD use.
33714842.release_evidence: The Python source code of the best performing implementation of XAOM is publicly available at https://github.com/fhrzic/XAOM.
33714842.headline_result: PCA alignment mean error 1.65 degrees; VGG16 orientation accuracy 0.993

33851261.clinical_problem: How can AI approaches successful in adult body MRI (image optimization, organ segmentation, osseous lesion detection) be adapted to pediatric body MRI?
33851261.model_description: Narrative review discussing non-interpretive and interpretive AI applications for pediatric body MRI, including image optimization, abdominal organ segmentation, and osseous lesion detection, drawing on adult body MRI AI literature.

33897363.exclusion_reason: AI mentioned only in passing as a future research need; review is about Zika virus neurobiology broadly, not an AI/imaging AI review

33900047.exclusion_reason: non-imaging (epidemiological air pollution exposure/asthma questionnaire study); random forest used only to estimate air pollution levels, not an imaging AI application

33904953.clinical_problem: How can AI tools assist in the prediction, identification, and investigation of child abuse in pediatric radiology practice?
33904953.model_description: Narrative review discussing potential and emerging roles of AI tools in identifying and investigating findings of child abuse on pediatric imaging.

33949048.model_family: dilated CNN combined with relational network (dilated CNN + RN)
33949048.clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion tractography connectome data, combined with psychometric data, predict expressive and receptive language scores in young children with persistent language concerns?
33949048.patient_population: 31 young children with persistent language concerns (mean age 4.25+/-2.38 years)
33949048.model_description: Takes diffusion tensor imaging-derived structural connectome features and psychometric data as input; a dilated CNN combined with a relational network outputs predicted expressive and receptive language scores.
33949048.headline_result: Pearson R 1.00 (expressive), 0.99 (receptive) between predicted and actual scores; MAE 0.28 for both

33966168.clinical_problem: Can voxel-wise uncertainty quantification improve the reliability of automated deep learning segmentation used to assess developmental dysplasia of the hip on 3D ultrasound?
33966168.model_description: Takes 3D hip ultrasound screening scans as input; a Bayesian 3D U-Net trained with a voxel-wise uncertainty-aware loss outputs segmentation of the ilium and acetabulum along with per-voxel confidence estimates.
33966168.headline_result: Dice score for ilium/acetabulum segmentation improved by 5% with the proposed uncertainty loss vs. standard cross-entropy loss

34020016.exclusion_reason: adult lifespan cognitive neuroscience study (ages spanning young adulthood to advanced age), not pediatric; primarily statistical/graph-theoretical fMRI analysis, not a diagnostic AI model

34026669.exclusion_reason: adult-only dataset (pediatric X-rays explicitly excluded from the training data)

34054117.exclusion_reason: non-imaging (serum biomarker and clinical variable prediction model via mixed graphical modeling); imaging tests noted only as recorded data, not model inputs

34059375.model_family: AI-based automated plane recognition and measurement algorithm (architecture unspecified)
34059375.clinical_problem: Can an AI-based ultrasound technique automatically recognize standard fetal planes and obtain biometric measurements to improve workflow efficiency during prenatal scanning?
34059375.patient_population: 1,005 uncomplicated singleton pregnancies, second and third trimesters
34059375.model_description: Takes live prenatal ultrasound video as input; the Smart Fetus AI technique automatically recognizes standard fetal planes (thalami, abdomen, femur) and outputs biometric measurements (biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length).
34059375.headline_result: Successful automatic acquisition in 99.30% of cases (998/1005); high agreement with traditional technique; significantly shorter scan time

34155718.clinical_problem: Can diffusion MRI-based myometrial tractography combined with anatomical MRI features improve prenatal detection of placenta accreta spectrum disorder?
34155718.patient_population: 47 pregnant women in the third trimester with PAS risk factors
34155718.model_description: Takes diffusion MRI tractography features and anatomical MRI features as input; a random forest model combines them to output a prediction of placenta accreta spectrum disorder.
34155718.headline_result: Integrated model AUC 0.880, accuracy 87.2%, vs. anatomical-only AUC 0.842

34198444.exclusion_reason: non-imaging (clinical/physical-examination-based fetal weight prediction using historical weight trajectory data, not ultrasound image analysis)

34220480.exclusion_reason: non-imaging (EEG signal-based prediction model), explicitly excluded modality; MRI mentioned only as a supplementary qualitative observation, not model input

34265208.exclusion_reason: non-imaging (prediction model uses anthropometric and bioelectrical impedance data, not image analysis; liver ultrasound used only as reference-standard label)

34332349.body_region: pelvis, humeral heads, femoral heads (iliac crests)
34332349.clinical_problem: Can a machine learning approach automate Risser sign skeletal maturity grading from EOS radiographs to reduce inter-observer variability in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis management?
34332349.model_description: Takes regions of interest (humeral heads, femoral heads, pelvis/iliac crests) from EOS radiographs as input; a ResNet101 CNN extracts image features, and an SVM classifier outputs the Risser sign skeletal maturity grade.

34496420.model_family: NLP + supervised ML (SVM, neural network, naive Bayes, decision tree, random forest, AdaBoost, KNN)
34496420.clinical_problem: Can machine learning automatically extract and classify the anatomical position of a peripherally inserted central catheter tip from radiology reports in infants, to flag noncentral catheter placement for clinicians?
34496420.patient_population: 17,337 radiographs from infants under 6 months of age with an upper extremity PICC
34496420.model_description: Takes free-text radiology report descriptions of PICC line tip location as input; NLP and supervised machine learning classifiers (best: SVM and neural network) output the catheter tip's anatomical location (central vs. noncentral, or one of 12 categories).
34496420.headline_result: Up to 98% accuracy for binary central/noncentral classification; up to 95% for 12-category classification

34507303.clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion MRI-derived white matter structural connectivity detect juvenile myoclonic epilepsy as a biomarker?
34507303.model_description: Takes white matter structural connectivity derived from diffusion MRI (Q-ball imaging, NODDI) as input; a transfer-learned deep convolutional neural network (Inception_resnet_v2) outputs classification of JME vs. normal control.
34507303.headline_result: Best JME detection accuracy 92.2% with Inception_resnet_v2 at 16% transfer rate
